guide.whatIsDesc: SiteScribe is a Change Order Copilot for construction projects. You upload evidence (site logs, photos, RFIs, plan revisions, contracts), the system detects potential changes (signals), you group them into events, create Change Order (CO) drafts—with optional AI help—then export PDF and evidence packages for approval.
guide.howItWorksDesc: The main workflow is: Evidence → Signals → Events → Change Order → Export. Everything in the app supports this path.
guide.gettingStartedDesc2: Sign in – Use the same credentials to log in.
guide.gettingStartedDesc3: Organizations – After login you land on Organizations. Create one or accept an invitation.
guide.gettingStartedDesc4: Projects – Inside an organization, create or open a project. All evidence, signals, and COs live inside a project.

hero.title: Evidence-backed
hero.subtitle: Turn site logs, RFIs, plan revisions, and photos into clear Change Order drafts. One place for evidence → signals → events → CO → export. Optional AI. No lock-in.
hero.noCard: No credit card. Open source. Self-host or use as-is.

problem.heading: Change Orders shouldn't be a mess
problem.subheading: Construction teams lose time and money when evidence and COs live in different worlds.
problem.card1Desc: Site logs, RFIs, plan revisions, and photos live in emails, drives, and paper. Linking them to a Change Order is manual and error-prone.
problem.card2Desc: Missing or scattered evidence slows approvals and fuels disputes. Owners and contractors waste time chasing documents instead of building.
problem.card3Desc: Change Orders are drafted in Word or spreadsheets with no direct tie to the evidence that supports scope, cost, and schedule.

solution.heading: One workflow: Evidence → CO → Export
solution.subheading: SiteScribe keeps evidence and Change Orders in one place so approvals are faster and disputes fewer.
solution.step1Body: Site logs, photos, RFIs, plan revisions, contracts. One project, one evidence store.
solution.step2Body: The app scans for change signals—keywords, plan revs, RFIs—and groups them into events.
solution.step3Body: You set event status, pick a template or use AI, and generate a Change Order draft linked to the event.
solution.step4Body: Edit the CO, add cost lines, enrich with AI if you want, then export PDF + ZIP with evidence and manifest.

forTeams.heading: Built for construction teams
forTeams.subheading: Whether you're a GC, sub, PM, or owner—evidence-backed Change Orders keep everyone aligned.
forTeams.gcDesc: Centralize evidence and COs across projects. Speed up owner approvals and reduce disputes.
forTeams.subTitle: Subcontractors
forTeams.subDesc: Document changes with evidence, submit clear CO drafts, and keep a traceable record.
forTeams.pmDesc: Run detection, triage events, and generate CO drafts without leaving one tool.
forTeams.ownerDesc: Review COs with linked evidence and manifest. Fewer surprises, faster sign-off.

features.heading: Everything you need for evidence-backed COs
features.subheading: From evidence to export, with optional AI and integrations. No vendor lock-in.
features.feature1Desc: Upload and link site logs, photos, RFIs, plan revisions, contracts. Link evidence to each other (e.g. RFI → plan revision) and compare plan revisions side by side.
features.feature2Desc: Scan recent evidence for change signals—keywords, plan revs, RFIs—and group them into events. Triage status and generate CO drafts from events.
features.feature3Desc: Edit scope, clauses, cost line items, schedule impact. Export PDF + ZIP with evidence and SHA-256 manifest. Optional mailto or email delivery.
features.feature4Desc: When enabled: CO draft and enrich from evidence, semantic search, signal scoring. Use Mistral (or compatible) API. Works without AI too.
features.feature5Desc: Reusable CO templates per organization. Pick a template when generating a draft from an event for consistent, fast COs.
features.feature6Desc: Cron-based automatic PDF+ZIP exports (e.g. weekly). Optional notification email. Integrate with Vercel Cron or any scheduler.
features.feature7Desc: Search across evidence and Change Orders. With AI: semantic search by meaning, not just keywords.
features.feature8Desc: Get notified when invited to an org or when a CO is created. Mark read / mark all read. Links take you to the right page.
features.feature9Desc: POST to your URL on co.created and co.status_changed. Integrate with Slack, ERP, or your own tools. Owner-only.
features.feature10Desc: Organizations with projects, members, and roles (VIEWER, SUBCONTRACTOR, FIELD, PM, OWNER). Invite by email and manage access.
features.feature11Desc: Add friends by username and chat one-to-one. Coordinate with teammates without leaving the app. Messages only between accepted friends; conversation list and read status included.

docs.introDesc: Everything you need to understand and use SiteScribe: what it is, why it exists, and how to use every feature step by step.
docs.whatIsP1: SiteScribe is an evidence-backed Change Order tool for construction. You upload evidence (site logs, photos, RFIs, plan revisions, contracts). The app helps you find possible changes (signals), group them into events, and create Change Order drafts. You then edit and export PDFs with evidence attached. AI is optional.
docs.whatIsP2: It is open source and free. You can use it as-is or self-host it.
docs.purposeP1: Purpose: To give construction teams one place to collect evidence, spot changes, and produce Change Orders that are clearly linked to that evidence. This speeds up approvals and reduces disputes.
docs.purposeP2: Who it's for: General contractors, subcontractors, project managers, and owners who need to document changes with evidence and produce clear CO drafts. Anyone who is tired of evidence in email and COs in Word with no direct link between them.
docs.gettingStartedP: Follow these steps to use SiteScribe from zero.
docs.gettingStartedL1: Register. Go to the app and create an account (email + password). No credit card.
docs.gettingStartedL2: Sign in. Use the same email and password to log in.
docs.gettingStartedL3: Create an organization. After login you see the Organizations page. Click "Create organization", give it a name and optional slug (e.g. my-company). The organization is your company or team.
docs.gettingStartedL4: Create a project. Open "Projects" from the menu, select your organization, then create a project. A project is one construction job. All evidence, signals, and Change Orders live inside a project.
docs.mainFlowP: The whole app is built around this path. You don't have to do every step every time, but this is the main flow.
docs.mainFlowL1: Evidence – Upload and optionally link documents and photos.
docs.mainFlowL2: Run detection – The app scans evidence for change signals (keywords, plan revs, RFIs) and groups them into events.
docs.mainFlowL3: Signals & events – You see a list of events, set status (Open, In progress, Done), and choose an event to create a CO draft.
docs.mainFlowL4: Generate CO draft – From an event you create a new Change Order (from a template or with AI).
docs.mainFlowL5: Edit CO – You edit title, scope, cost lines, schedule impact, and status.
docs.mainFlowL6: Export – You export a PDF of the CO and a ZIP of evidence (with a manifest). You can send it by email or mailto.
docs.orgP: An organization is your company or team. It has projects, members, and (if you are OWNER) webhooks. You can have more than one organization.
docs.orgL1: From the Organizations page, click "Create organization". Enter name and optional slug.
docs.orgL2: As OWNER, you can invite people by email and choose their role. They get a link to accept the invite.
docs.orgL3: Only OWNERs can add webhooks and manage invitations.
docs.orgR1: VIEWER – Can only view evidence, signals, COs, exports.
docs.orgR3: FIELD – Can upload evidence, export COs, add comments.
docs.orgR4: PM – Can run detection, triage events, create and edit CO drafts, manage the project.
docs.orgR5: OWNER – Can do everything in the org (invite, webhooks) and all PM actions in its projects.
docs.projectsP: A project is one construction job. Inside a project you have: evidence, evidence links, plan compare, signals and events, search, Change Orders, exports, templates, and scheduled exports.
docs.projectsL1: Go to Projects in the menu, select an organization, then click to create a new project (name and optional description).
docs.projectsL2: Open a project to see its Overview: short summary and recent events, with links to Evidence and Signals.
docs.projectsL3: Use the project sidebar to open Dashboard, Evidence, Evidence links, Plan compare, Signals, Search, Exports, Templates, and Scheduled exports.
docs.evidenceP: Evidence is the raw material: documents and photos that support a change. You upload files or paste text. The app stores them in the project and can use them for search and signal detection.
docs.evidenceT1: Site log – Daily or periodic log (text or file).
docs.evidenceL1: Open the project → Evidence. Click "Add evidence" (or similar). Choose type, add title and date, then upload a file or paste text.
docs.evidenceL2: PDFs are processed so you can search their text and use them in signal detection.
docs.evidenceL3: Evidence links – In "Evidence links" you can link two evidence items (e.g. "this RFI references that plan revision") with an optional link type.
docs.evidenceL4: Plan compare – In "Plan compare" you select two plan-revision evidence items to view them side by side.
docs.signalsP: Signal detection scans recent evidence (e.g. last 30 days) for hints of change: keywords (e.g. "revision", "delay", "change order"), plan revisions, RFIs. Each hit is a signal. Signals are grouped into events (by date and type). You triage events and generate CO drafts from them.
docs.signalsL1: Open the project → Signals. Click Run detection. The app scans evidence and creates/updates events.
docs.signalsL2: You see a list of events. Each has a status (Open, In progress, Done). Change the status from the dropdown on the card.
docs.signalsL3: Click an event to open its page. There you see the evidence timeline and a button to Generate CO draft (from a template or with AI). That creates a new Change Order linked to the event.
docs.coP: A Change Order is the formal document for a scope/cost/schedule change. You create a draft from an event (template or AI), then edit it in the CO editor. You can add cost line items, comments, and export PDF + ZIP.
docs.coF1: Title, scope narrative, contract clause references, assumptions, exclusions.
docs.coF3: Cost line items: description, quantity, unit, unit price, amount. You can add multiple rows.
docs.coL1: From an event page, click Generate CO draft. Choose "From template" or "With AI". A new CO is created; open it from the link or from the project.
docs.coL2: On the CO page you edit all fields. Use Add line for cost items. Click Save when done.
docs.coL3: If AI is enabled, Enrich with AI can fill or improve scope, clauses, and cost from the linked evidence.
docs.coL4: Comments – Add comments on the CO for discussion. They appear below the editor.
docs.coL5: Export – Use "Export PDF + ZIP" to download the CO PDF and a ZIP of evidence with a manifest. You can also use "Export + mailto" or send by email if configured.
docs.searchP: From the project Search page you search across evidence and Change Orders. The app does full-text search in titles, descriptions, and extracted text. If AI is enabled, semantic search is also available: you search by meaning and get matches by similarity.
docs.searchL1: Open the project → Search. Enter a query and run the search.
docs.searchL2: Results are shown in two groups: Evidence and Change Orders. Click a result to go to the evidence list or the CO page.
docs.searchL3: If semantic search is on, you may see an extra "Semantic search (AI)" section with meaning-based matches.
docs.exportsP: Exports are packages tied to a CO: a PDF of the CO and a ZIP of linked evidence files plus a manifest (with file hashes). You create them from the CO page with "Export PDF + ZIP".
docs.exportsL1: Open a Change Order → click Export PDF + ZIP. The app generates the package. You can then download the PDF and ZIP from the CO page or from the project Exports list.
docs.exportsL2: In the project → Exports you see all past exports with links to download PDF and ZIP.
docs.exportsL3: Export + mailto – Opens your email client with the package attached or linked. Export by email – Enter an email address and the app can send the export (if email is configured).
docs.templatesP: CO templates are reusable blueprints (name + optional body and cost line JSON). You create them per organization from the project Templates page. When you generate a CO draft from an event, you can pick a template to pre-fill the CO.
docs.templatesL1: Open the project → Templates. Create a new template: name, optional body text, optional cost line items (JSON).
docs.templatesL2: When you click "Generate CO draft" on an event, choose "From template" and select a template. The new CO is pre-filled with that content.
docs.scheduledP: Scheduled exports run automatically on a schedule (cron). You choose: which project, which CO (or all COs), and optional email to notify when the export is done. The server exposes an API that a cron job (e.g. Vercel Cron) calls with a secret.
docs.scheduledL1: Open the project → Scheduled exports. Add a new schedule: cron expression (e.g. 0 9 * * 1 for every Monday 09:00), choose one CO or all COs, optional notification email.
docs.scheduledL2: Configure your cron service to call the app's scheduled-export API with the secret. Each schedule can be enabled/disabled or deleted from the list.
docs.notificationsP: The app can create notifications for you (e.g. when you are invited to an org, or when a CO is created). You open Notifications from the main menu (or the bell link in the project sidebar) to see the list.
docs.notificationsL1: Click Notifications in the nav. You see all notifications. Click "Mark all as read" or mark a single one as read.
docs.notificationsL2: Each notification can link to the relevant page (e.g. accept invite, CO page). Click the title to go there.
docs.webhooksP: Webhooks are HTTP POST calls the app sends to a URL you provide when something happens. Supported events: co.created, co.status_changed. Only organization OWNERs can add webhooks.
docs.webhooksL1: Go to Organizations → open your org → Webhooks (or go to the webhooks page and select the org).
docs.webhooksL2: Add a webhook: URL and optional secret. The app will POST to that URL when a CO is created or its status changes. Use this to integrate with Slack, ERP, or your own tools.
docs.aiP: If the app is configured with ENABLE_AI=true and an API key (e.g. Mistral), you get optional AI features. The app works fully without AI too.
docs.aiL1: CO draft and enrich – Generate CO text from evidence, or enrich an existing CO with AI-suggested scope, clauses, cost/schedule.
docs.aiL2: Evidence – Suggested type, title, summary; embeddings for semantic search.
docs.aiL3: Semantic search – Search by meaning (embedding similarity).
docs.aiL4: Signals – LLM scoring and reasoning per signal.
docs.quickRefE: Evidence types: Site log, Photo, RFI (PDF), Plan revision (PDF), Contract (PDF).
docs.quickRefR: Roles: VIEWER → SUBCONTRACTOR → FIELD → PM → OWNER (increasing permissions).
docs.quickRefF: Flow: Evidence → Run detection → Events → Generate CO draft → Edit CO → Export PDF + ZIP.
docs.quickRefX: Export: PDF (CO) + ZIP (evidence + manifest with SHA-256).
